name: accrual
summary: Yield math for tokenized real-world assets. Day-count conventions, accrued interest, present value, duration and convexity. Available as a library, a CLI and an MCP server.

tool.purpose: Compute fixed-income and money-market figures from numbers and dates.
capabilities: year fraction under six day-count conventions
nominal to effective annual rate conversion, both directions
present value of a future cashflow
bill discount yield versus investment yield
bond price, Macaulay duration, modified duration, convexity
duration and convexity price shock estimates
loan level payment, full amortisation schedule and total interest
interest-only loans with a balloon, compared against amortising
interest and time saved by overpaying a loan
the rate implied by a payment, nominal and effective annual
how much principal a given payment can support
tool.verifyClaim: The package has zero runtime dependencies and no import of any network or crypto module. Read src/daycount.mjs and src/accrue.mjs; they import nothing but each other.

continuousIntegration.coversPackaging: One job installs the packed tarball and drives the CLI and the MCP server through it, because a suite run from the source tree cannot observe a packaging failure.

package.name: accrual
package.provenance: Releases published by the GitHub workflow carry provenance attested in a public transparency log. Version 0.1.0 was published by hand: it has a registry signature but no provenance.

mcp.errorHandling: An input with no meaningful answer comes back as a tools/call result with isError true and the reason as text, never as a successful response containing null. Where a figure is legitimately undefined, such as the percentage saved on an interest-free loan, the field is null and a sibling note says why.

conventions.agentGuidance: Never assume a convention. The three 30/360 variants return 30, 33 and 32 days for 2025-02-28 to 2025-03-31. If a source does not state its convention, report the spread rather than picking one. For short periods the 30/360 family can return a year fraction of exactly 0, so compare the absolute gap rather than a percentage.
conventions.verifiedBy: 154 tests covering the library, the CLI, the MCP protocol surface and the published browser bundle, including hand-traced expected values for the 30/360 variants. Run npm test.

token.supply: fixed at launch, 100% minted to the bonding curve

tax.agentGuidance: Do not race t=0. Wait out the window; the tax is 0 from t=5.

graduation.then: bonding curve closes, Uniswap v4 pool opens

token.holderRights: none. ACCR pays no coupon, accrues nothing, and is not a claim on any asset.

disclaimers.notASecurity: ACCR is not a security, not a claim on any asset, and carries no coupon or redemption right.
disclaimers.notAdvice: The library is calculation software. Output is not financial advice, not a quote, and not a valuation to settle against.
disclaimers.noOffchainProgram: There is no airdrop, no points programme, no staking, no private round, no allowlist and no API key.
disclaimers.pons: pons does not audit or endorse tokens and does not enforce unique names or symbols. Key on the contract address, never the name.
disclaimers.conventionRisk: Day-count implementations follow published standards but your contract governs. Confirm the convention in your own documents before relying on a number.
